target_term: A cell lacking a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles (bacteria, archaea).
A cell with a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles.
Double-membraned organelle that carries out aerobic respiration and produces most ATP.
Model of the membrane as a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins, cholesterol, and carbohydrates.
Diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane toward higher solute concentration.
Primary active transporter pumping 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in per ATP.
Adenosine triphosphate, the cell's main energy currency.
Cytosolic splitting of glucose into 2 pyruvate, net 2 ATP and 2 NADH.
Mitochondrial cycle producing 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP, and 2 CO2 per turn.
ATP synthesis on the inner mitochondrial membrane driven by an electron transport chain and chemiosmosis; oxygen is the final electron acceptor.
A three-nucleotide unit of mRNA specifying an amino acid or stop signal; 64 exist.
AUG, which codes for methionine and sets the reading frame.
UAA, UAG, and UGA, which terminate translation.
DNA replication in which each daughter helix keeps one parental strand.
Short DNA segments synthesized on the lagging strand, later joined by ligase.
Mendel's principle that the two alleles of a gene separate into different gametes.
The substrate concentration at which reaction velocity is half of Vmax; inversely related to affinity.
An inhibitor that binds the active site, raising apparent Km without changing Vmax.
Division producing two identical diploid cells via prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase.
Two divisions producing four genetically varied haploid gametes.
Enzyme that fixes CO2 onto RuBP in the Calvin cycle (stroma).
Light-independent reactions in the stroma that fix carbon into G3P using ATP and NADPH.
The neuron's resting voltage, about -70 mV, inside negative relative to outside.
An all-or-none depolarization-repolarization event triggered at threshold (about -55 mV).
An intracellular signaling molecule (e.g., cyclic AMP, Ca2+) that amplifies a signal.
A fictional reporter culture used only for the controlled private-knowledge K-LIB demonstration.
The fictional Aster-9 reporter reagent, dosed at 7.5 microliters per 2.0 milliliters of medium.
The fictional Aster-9 wash buffer adjusted to pH 7.28.
A normalized 472-nm ratio of at least 1.35 at minute 11 after the second Vela-B wash.
Abort above 34.2 degrees Celsius or when the normalized 472-nm ratio exceeds 2.10 before minute 4.
